title: What You Can Promise Alone — Libraries That Agree in the End
description: Highly available transactions told in the reading rooms of the scholars' coast of Paxos: what a library can promise a reader who consults and corrects its compendium while the couriers are stopped, what needs the reader to stay with one library, and what no library can promise alone.
question: When a machine cannot stop to check with the others on every change, what can it still promise on its own? That no one sees a reply before the message it answers? That no one sees a change half made? That two people never take the last item?
how: We find out by exploring what the libraries of the scholars' coast could still promise the readers of their compendium on days when the couriers between them stopped running.

papers.authors: Peter Bailis, Aaron Davidson, Alan Fekete, Ali Ghodsi, Joseph M. Hellerstein and Ion Stoica
papers.title: Highly Available Transactions: Virtues and Limitations
